dossier_meta.catalog_title: Open Question: bounded twin-width for sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs
dossier_meta.statement_text: Is there a function $f:\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every $\mathcal{O}_{k}$-free graph that does not contain $K_{t,t}$ as a subgraph has twin-width at most $f(t,k)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper shows that sparse $\mathcal{O}_k$-free graphs have logarithmic treewidth, but leaves open whether their twin-width is also bounded as a function of $t$ and $k$. The authors note that $\mathcal{O}_2$-free graphs without $K_{3,3}$ already yield a new family of counterexamples to bounded treewidth from forbidden induced subgraphs alone.
